findings.summary: The review-ledger and activation-baseline validators defaulted to their permissive branch, so an omitted cross-document input passed silently.
evidence: validate_review_ledger(prior_ledger=None, strict_freshness=False) and validate_temporary_activation_baseline(prior_baseline=None, current_violation_ids=None) skipped append-only detection, final-review staleness, and the new-violation check, while validate_property_registry deliberately raised uncertainty for the same omission.
requirement_property: Integration-plan §3.3 (an unretrievable prior registry reports uncertainty rather than silently accepting rewritten history)
resolution_evidence: Both now use the _NOT_PROVIDED sentinel and raise typed uncertainty in strict mode; strict_activation is deliberately excluded because it adds a requirement rather than relaxing one.

findings.summary: No schema declared $id, so every relative $ref lacked a base URI.
evidence: All ten schemas declared $schema but omitted $id while carrying 111+ relative cross-file refs; resolution worked only under a filename-keyed loader, and the candidate's own reference test resolved by filename lookup so it could not detect this.
requirement_property: Integration-plan §3.1 (A2 freezes versioned schemas as machine contracts a different producer can consume)
resolution_evidence: Every schema pins a canonical non-dereferenceable $id; the bounded validator resolves refs by RFC 3986 against it and refuses a schema set in which any document omits one.

findings.summary: A property registered under an FR-CS-/FR-TS- id silently captured that requirement's waiver authority.
evidence: exception_route evaluates its property branch first and unconditionally. With a property registered as FR-CS-046, exception_route('FR-CS-046') returned route 'governance-property' with governance_exception_allowed True, routing a Code Standards waiver into exceptions.json. property_id carried no namespace constraint in schema or code.
requirement_property: Integration-plan §3.6 -- this integration MUST NOT route FR-CS or FR-TS waivers directly into exceptions.json
resolution_evidence: property_id in a #19/#20 namespace is now rejected in both the schema and the semantics from one control-data source; §3.6's carve-out survives because an admitted property cites the FR requirement instead of taking its id.
